pushback_verification: All 6 verified against current state before disposition (during the evaluation turn and at walk time); none stale. The selector-less `gh pr view` was reproduced against the real CLI and the corrected form checked the same way; the recovery bullet, the requirement prose and scenario, task 3.1a, the full onboarding sentence, the diff call's discarded status, and the harness's `absent` handling were each read at their cited lines.

resolutions.title: The archive state-observation command lacks the selector required with --repo
resolutions.action: Reproduced (`argument required when using the --repo flag`). Tail step 4 now reads `gh pr view --repo <owner>/<repo> <url> --json isDraft`, addressing the PR by the URL step 2 validated or step 3 discovered, with the selector named as REQUIRED and the observation stated as independent of the checkout branch; the corrected form is accepted by the real CLI (it reaches GitHub). The fidelity sweep gained a selector rule: every selector-taking `gh pr` verb (view/edit/ready/merge/close/reopen/checkout) must carry `<url>` or `<number>` after `--repo <owner>/<repo>` — `--repo` alone is no longer accepted as qualification. Archive and architect reference hashes re-pinned.

resolutions.title: The archive spec's recovery command still bypasses commit isolation
resolutions.action: The failure-branch recovery bullet now prescribes `git add <paths> && git commit --only <paths>` and states why (a plain `git commit` in recovery would publish the whole index, defeating the ratified isolation on exactly the path a user follows by hand). The reference's own recovery bullet already carried `--only`; the spec now agrees. No scenario carried the old form (grep-verified).

resolutions.title: The normative repository-qualification rule still requires the rejected flag form
resolutions.action: Swept the WHOLE requirement, not the example: the prose now says qualification is IN THE GRAMMAR EACH COMMAND ACCEPTS (`--repo` on the `gh pr` verbs; positional on `gh repo view`, which has no `--repo` flag; selector-taking verbs additionally carry the PR's URL or number); the fork-checkout scenario says the same; task 3.1a reworded with a dated note that its universal-flag wording was the invalid grammar's last surviving statement. `grep 'on EVERY .gh. invocation'` now hits only the corrected sentence.

resolutions.title: Onboarding teaches that stage archive flips program PRs READY
resolutions.action: The archive teach-in now splits PER GRANULARITY: per-change PR — rewrite the description and flip READY; program PR — append this stage's entry and flip NOTHING, stage archives never flip the program PR, its READY flip is the human's act at arc-done where the architect readout surfaces it. A fidelity assertion pins the split on the onboarding body and asserts the old unconditional sentence is gone. Onboard hashes re-pinned.

resolutions.title: The phase-1 transcription treats a failed compatibility diff as an empty compatible diff
resolutions.action: The per-proposal path test now requires the diff to RESOLVE: a non-zero `git diff <default>...<tip>` exit (no merge base — an unrelated root) is a named collision skip, never an empty compatible diff. The reference's compatibility bullet states the failed-observation rule (a failed observation is a skip, not a pass). Regression case: a same-named orphan branch with a foreign file skips with `no merge base` in the note, HEAD unmoved on main, and the foreign file never exposed.

resolutions.title: The phase-1 transcription can create a branch with gh genuinely absent
resolutions.action: The reference's resolution section gained `gh availability — checked FIRST, before any branch work`: an absent `gh` takes the degraded path with no branch created, switched, or fast-forwarded, and a missing executable is a distinct fact from an installed CLI whose query fails — the symbolic-ref fallback is now stated as ONLY for the latter. The transcription probes `gh --version` on the repo's PATH before default-branch resolution and skips on ENOENT or non-zero. The harness's `gh: 'absent'` now builds a PATH of the (empty) stub dir plus `/usr/bin:/bin` — git present, no host `gh` — via a new `envPath` field every command honors. Regression case: absent gh + a resolvable remote HEAD → skip naming gh, HEAD on main, no branch created.

Onboarding now teaches the per-granularity tail with a fidelity pin. The transcription gates on gh availability before any branch work and the harness's absent mode is genuinely absent. 2008 -> 2011 tests green across 91 files; six parity hash lines re-pinned across five templates; local surface refreshed and verified; strict-valid; fingerprints 5/5.
